title: Profile of Employees Retrenched due to COVID-19 Pandemic
what_it_is: Profile of Employees Retrenched due to COVID-19 Pandemic

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits and Singaporeans
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Manpower about guidelines on excess manpower, retrenchment numbers by service length, benefit amounts, and legislating a baseline retrenchment benefit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether she can clarify how the national guidelines on managing excess manpower and responsible retrenchments and other related policies ensure that Singaporeans are better off compared to permanent residents and non-Singaporeans in terms of job and income security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower of the total retrenchments of 11,350 workers in the first half of 2020, (a) what is (i) the number of workers with less than two years' service with the company versus at least two years' service and (ii) the median and range of the retrenchment benefit based on the number of months' of salary for every year of service; and (b) whether a baseline retrenchment benefit can be legislated.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefit notifications
sections.summary: Notifications from April to September show about two-thirds of retrenched employees had at least two years' service and were eligible for benefits, with about nine in 10 receiving some benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Based on notifications received between April and September this year, about two-thirds of the employees affected by retrenchment had at least two years of service with their employers and were eligible for retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: About nine in 10 of these eligible employees received some retrenchment benefit, of which about 84% received at least two weeks' salary per year of service.

sections.label: Part-time re-employment for older workers
sections.summary: The Part-time Re-employment Grant provides up to $125,000 to companies committing to a part-time re-employment policy, and resident employment rate for those aged 60 and above rose from 27.2% in 2009 to 38.5% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To encourage more employers to offer part-time opportunities for them and enable them to stay on in the workforce, we introduced the Part-time Re-employment Grant earlier this year that will provide up to $125,000 to companies that commit to a part-time re-employment policy.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our employment rate for residents aged 60 and above has increased from 27.2% in 2009 to 38.5% in 2019.
